widgets_values:
Animate the upright bipedal golden tiger mount carrying its original seated rider from the single reference image as a seamless repeating running-in-place game animation.

Keep the exact original REAR FOLLOW camera throughout. We see the rider and mount FROM BEHIND, facing directly away. Feet cycle away from the viewer while the whole character stays in place. Never reveal a front face, side profile or orbit the camera.

The tiger RUNS ON ITS TWO HIND LEGS exactly as its bipedal reference anatomy: alternate left and right hind feet with distinct push-off and lifted-knee phases. Its short forearms swing slightly. Keep the seated rider attached to the saddle; the rider does not run independently.

Sustain a steady complete repeated motion from the start through the end, with matching stride phase at the loop boundary. Keep the head and torso proportions constant. The mount's original body and rider must stay recognizable in every frame. Do not merely slide or shake a static picture.

Anchor the entire character group at the exact original horizontal center and ground level. Preserve the original character size relative to the square canvas and all empty margins. Use only small natural gait motion; do not enlarge, recenter, shrink or crop the subject. Keep every ear, foot, tail, saddle, rider, hair and accessory within the frame. Fixed camera: no zoom, pan, tracking, orbit, cuts, shake or reframing. Preserve the exact rider identity, costume, face, hairstyle, colors, mount anatomy, equipment and illustrated 2D rendering style.

Keep a perfectly flat uniform solid magenta background, #FF00FF, for every frame. No scenery, floor, cast shadow, text, added characters, new equipment, motion blur, dust, smoke, trails, flashes or new magic effects. Preserve only effects that already belong to the reference. No speech or music.

widgets_values_named.prompt:
Animate the single SD warrior from the input image performing one spectacular three-strike sword ultimate toward screen-right. Keep the original front three-quarter view. Build the spectacle through decisive body movement and the actual sword, without added visual effects.

0.0-0.7 seconds: sink into a low stance, load the rear leg, rotate the hips and shoulders slightly, and draw the sword close to the weapon-side hip. Keep the face readable and the free hand in a strong balancing pose.
0.7-1.5 seconds: drive a fast rising diagonal slash toward screen-right using a short planted step and coordinated hip rotation. Keep the sword elbow bent enough to preserve clearance from the right edge.
1.5-2.4 seconds: immediately reverse into a forceful descending diagonal slash. Lower the center of gravity, pivot on the feet, and let the hair and cloth follow with a natural delay. Make this a distinct second strike, with a brief readable follow-through.
2.4-3.5 seconds: recoil into a compact crouch, perform a low hop with both feet briefly leaving the ground, and deliver the third and strongest downward slash while landing firmly near the starting position. Keep the jump low and the blade arc close to the body. Finish in a powerful low pose for a short beat.
3.5-5.0 seconds: recover smoothly to the original position, viewing angle, and ready stance. Perform exactly three distinct strikes, with no extra swings, full spins, or travel across the screen.

Preserve the original face, eyepatch, hair, blue-and-gold armor, ornamentation, sturdy SD proportions, and original sword hand. Keep the physical sword's exact original shape and length throughout; never stretch it during extension. Use a locked camera and unchanged character scale and canvas framing. Keep the whole body, hair, cloth, and sword tip inside the frame with visible clearance from every edge throughout each strike. Use the original plain uniform background. Only the warrior and his existing equipment appear. No enemy, added weapon, sword trails, afterimages, speed lines, wind-pressure effects, gusts, shockwaves, energy slashes, glow, flashes, particles, smoke, dust, or camera shake. No dialogue or music.

widgets_values:
Vaporwave title sequence look: pink and blue gradient palette, VHS tracking artifacts, Greek statue motifs, chrome palm trees, RGB chromatic aberration, lo-fi retro atmosphere, mood languid and nostalgic.

Timeline:
[0s-1s] VHS static opens the frame, the title "COMFYUI" appears with RGB split and a slight horizontal jitter.
[1s-2.5s] Hard cut, a Greek plaster bust close-up, pink-purple gradient sky, a pixelated sun.
[2.5s-4s] Clean "STARRING" credits appear, "LATENT" and "CONTROLNET" each shown exactly once.
[4s-5s] Final card "DIRECTED BY COMFYUI" holds, one VHS tracking glitch settling into stability.

Hard cuts only, transitions landing with tape jumps, no push-ins, no dissolves.

Audio: lo-fi vaporwave score, slow drum machine with soft bass, VHS tape-noise sample joins at 2.5s, melody fading for the last 1s.

All text must be clearly legible, do not misspell English, no Chinese characters, do not repeat names or job titles, no soft dissolves, no subtitle bars.
